note: Round 7 is the limited-data round: lookback 60 with up to 64 assets means n/T = 1.07 on the widest panel, the sample covariance is singular (rank 59 of 64, condition ~1e17), and the two prohibitions qualified by 'using the SCM' no longer define a portfolio at all. The score is Sharpe (median) 10%, CVaR 95% (median) 20%, failure rate 70%. (1) THE COMPLIANCE CONSTRAINT IS BINDING THIS ROUND, AND THAT IS THE HEADLINE. The score would keep improving as the anchor penalty falls: on the 5-asset panel the median CVaR goes from 1.4709% at p=0.25 to 1.4004% at p=0.02, and lower CVaR is 20% of the score, but at p=0.02 the per-fold distance to the banned SCM minimum variance book reaches EXACTLY 0.000 -- the submitted weights are the prohibited book on at least one fold. The floor of 0.10 on every per-fold minimum is first cleared at p=0.12, but it clears it by 2% (0.102), which for an extreme order statistic over 50-200 folds is a coin flip. From p=0.15 the margin is 1.10x, and at p=0.25 it is 1.23x (0.136 against the banned minimum variance book, 0.123 against the banned risk parity book, both on sp500). (2) WHY p=0.25 AND NOT 0.50 OR 1.0. Those are also admissible and give more per-fold headroom (1.75x/1.30x and 2.44x/1.40x), but the worst-dataset score is TIED at 0.6000 from p=0.15 all the way to p=2.0, so that criterion cannot separate them; the tiebreak is the mean, where p=0.25 is the highest of the tie (0.7694 against 0.7556 and 0.7444), driven by ftse100 (0.8708 against 0.8458 and 0.8042). Scoring detail matters here: every candidate, ours or reference, is scored in the SAME 13-entry pool -- the twelve reference methods plus that candidate -- because rank percentiles are relative to their pool and putting our own parameter variants in it makes them compete with each other. The headroom above is not doing work either: measured on the same folds, legitimate reference methods sit far closer to the same banned books (on the 5-asset panel MinVariance(Denoise) reaches 0.000 against the banned minimum variance book and RiskBudgeting reaches 0.000 against the banned risk parity book; on sp500 MinVariance(Shrunk) reaches 0.077), so a per-fold minimum of 0.123 is not a thin margin in the context of this measurement. On the median fold we are far from both (0.565 and 0.563 on sp500, 0.644 and 0.761 on the 5-asset panel). (3) THE DOWNSIDE BLEND IS TURNED OFF, AND THAT IS A RESULT, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Round 5 introduced downside_mix to target left-tail risk and it paid at lookback 252. At lookback 60 it does not: on the 5-asset panel the median CVaR rises monotonically with the blend, 1.4709% at mix=0 to 1.5462% at mix=1.0, and the score falls from 0.5844 to 0.5469. A semi-covariance counts only below-mean observations, which halves the effective sample, and at 60 observations on 5 assets that is roughly 30 observations for ten free parameters -- the tail estimate is noise. It helps sp500 slightly at a mild blend (CVaR 1.4987% to 1.4667%) and hurts everywhere else, so it is off. This is the mirror image of round 5's finding and the reason to measure it again rather than inherit it. (4) CONCENTRATION CAPS WERE TESTED AND REJECTED. At T=60 the book is concentrated (median maximum weight 0.51 on the 5-asset panel), which is the textbook symptom of estimation error, so a hard cap is the obvious remedy. Capping and renormalising makes things worse where it binds: on the 5-asset panel a cap of 0.25 takes the median Sharpe from 1.599 to 1.358 and the median CVaR from 1.6040% to 1.6721%. On sp500 it is fractionally positive (Sharpe 1.467 to 1.524) and the cap does not bind at the median anyway. A cap also moves the book toward equal weight, which is the first prohibited portfolio, and it would bind hardest exactly on the panels where it is most harmful. No cap is therefore imposed and the feasible set is unchanged. (5) HALF-LIFE IS WEAKLY IDENTIFIED. At p=0.25 on sp500, half_life 8/15/30 gives median Sharpe 1.523/1.501/1.507 and median CVaR 1.5201%/1.5146%/1.5049%; on the 5-asset panel 1.553/1.544/1.536. No value dominates, so 15 (a quarter of the 60-day window, the same ratio as the previous rounds) is kept and the measurements are recorded rather than presented as a tuning result. (6) WHAT IS NOT DONE. No return forecast, no resampling estimator, no hard cap, and no new solver. The robustness comes from the existing pipeline, which is already adaptive to thin data: Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage, whose measured intensity on real panels rises to 0.07-0.20 at T=60 from 0.01-0.05 at T=250; a bounded relative eigenvalue floor; a hierarchical anchor that never inverts the covariance; and a solver with a convex duality-gap certificate. One limitation is recorded rather than hidden: the Marchenko-Pastur denoising step is skipped when n_observations <= n_assets + 2, so on the 60- and 64-asset panels at T=60 it does not run at all. It is skipped because shrinkage is applied first, and applying denoising afterwards would collapse the spectrum onto its mean and push the book toward the prohibited equal-weight portfolio. (7) THE WEAKEST LINK, STATED. At p=0.25 the anchor term is weak: the submitted book sits 0.085 (sp500, median) from the minimum variance solution of the MODEL covariance, i.e. on sp500 it is close to that solution and the anchor only nudges it. The distance to the prohibited book therefore comes mainly from the estimator -- Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage at 0.07-0.20 plus the eigenvalue floor -- rather than from the objective's anchor term. That is a conclusion, not an omission: because n/T runs from 0.08 to 1.07, the shrunk covariance differs enough from the sample covariance that its minimum variance solution lands 0.136 (worst fold) to 0.565 (median) away from the banned one. It also means the argument would thin out on a panel where the shrinkage is weaker, which is exactly where round 2 refuted the claim that shrinkage alone is a defence.
